item.title: Bizarre Deep Sea Creatures Caught Hitchhiking on Giant Sea Spiders in the Deep Blue Sea
item.dc:creator: Dulaksha Sandeepa
item.description: Thousands of meters beneath the surface, where sunlight never penetrates the crushing depths of the deep blue sea, life adapts in ways that continuously defy conventional biology. While most ocean researchers focus on bioluminescent cephalopods or pelagic deep sea fish to understand the abyss, marine biologists exploring the southeastern Pacific Ocean have documented an unexpected ecological partnership: tiny, shrimp-like deep sea creatures deliberately hitchhiking on the bodies of colossal giant sea spiders.

item.title: Massive New Moon Crater Discovered by NASA: Inside the 'Once-in-a-Century' Asteroid Impact

item.description: In a planetary science breakthrough that rewrites our understanding of the lunar surface, NASA scientists have confirmed the discovery of the largest newly formed impact crater ever recorded across the modern solar system. Dubbed the McGetchin crater, the colossal chasm measures roughly 728 feet (222 meters) wide and up to 141 feet (43 meters) deep—the result of a rare once-in-a-century asteroid collision.

item.description: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman publicly declares that Pluto should be restored to planetary status, reigniting the decades-old debate over the dwarf planet's classification and Pluto's place in our solar system.

item.title: A New Study on the Origin of 3I/ATLAS
item.dc:creator: Astronomy Correspondent
item.description: Astronomers reveal that the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS originated from an extremely cold and isolated region of the Milky Way and may be the oldest interstellar object ever encountered at approximately 11 billion years old.

media:content.media:title: A New Study on the Origin of 3I/ATLAS

item.title: Can a Proposed Giant Dam Across the Ocean Save AMOC?
item.dc:creator: Climate & Engineering Correspondent
item.description: Scientists propose constructing a massive 51-mile dam across the Bering Strait to prevent the collapse of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, though significant technical, environmental, and geopolitical challenges remain.

media:content.media:title: Can a Proposed Giant Dam Across the Ocean Save AMOC?

item.title: Risk of Atlantic Ocean Current System Collapse on the Rise
item.dc:creator: Climate Research Correspondent
item.description: Latest scientific research reveals that the risk of collapse of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is significantly higher than previously estimated, with new data putting the probability well above 50%.

media:content.media:title: Risk of Atlantic Ocean Current System Collapse on the Rise

item.title: SpaceX Starlink Surpasses 10,000 Satellites in Low Earth Orbit — A Historic Milestone With Growing Concerns
item.dc:creator: SpaceX & International Space Community
item.description: SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet constellation has crossed a remarkable threshold, surpassing 10,000 active satellites in low Earth orbit as of March 17, 2026. The milestone brings unprecedented global connectivity but raises serious environmental and scientific concerns about ozone depletion, light pollution, and catastrophic collision risks.

media:content.media:title: SpaceX Starlink Surpasses 10,000 Satellites in Low Earth Orbit — A Historic Milestone With Growing Concerns

item.dc:creator: NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Team

item.dc:creator: Spaceflight Analysis Desk / China Manned Space Agency (CMSA)

item.dc:creator: Andrew McCarthy
item.description: An astrophotographer has successfully captured an extraordinary rare photograph of a skydiver falling freely from the sky, perfectly aligned with the surface of the Sun's face, creating an appearance as if an astronaut is falling toward the Sun.

item.title: Oldest RNA Molecules Ever Discovered Reveal Death Scene of Baby Mammoth
item.dc:creator: Centre for Palaeogenetics Research Team
item.description: Scientists have successfully extracted RNA molecules from the body of Yuka, a young mammoth that died approximately 40,000 years ago in what is now Siberia, revealing the biological processes occurring at the moment of death.

media:content.media:title: Oldest RNA Molecules Ever Discovered Reveal Death Scene of Baby Mammoth

item.dc:creator: National Weather Service Space Weather Prediction Center
item.description: Over the course of two nights, spectacular Northern Lights conditions were visible in unexpected locations, including areas as far south as Florida in the United States, caused by a massive dual solar storm.

item.title: Ryugu Asteroid Reveals It Once Contained Liquid Water
item.dc:creator: Tokyo University Research Team
item.description: With indications that large volumes of water once flowed inside the asteroid Ryugu, it appears that asteroids may have brought much more water to Earth than previously thought.

media:content.media:title: Ryugu Asteroid Reveals It Once Contained Liquid Water

item.dc:creator: Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory
item.description: American Nobel laureate James Watson, one of the two scientists who discovered the structure of DNA, has passed away at the age of 97.

item.dc:creator: NASA Space Agency & International Astronomical Community
item.description: Discovery of 3I/ATLAS - the third confirmed interstellar comet from another star system. Learn about this historic space discovery, its hyperbolic orbit, closest approach to Earth, and what NASA astronomers discovered about this interstellar object traveling at 221,000 kilometers per hour.

media:content.media:title: 3I/ATLAS Interstellar Comet: Historic Visitor from Outer Space Reaches Solar System

item.title: Japan's HTV-X Cargo Vehicle Launches First Mission to International Space Station
item.dc:creator: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA)
item.description: Japan's next-generation HTV-X cargo transport vehicle successfully launched on October 25, 2025, from Tanegashima Space Center aboard the H3 rocket. Scheduled to dock with the ISS on October 29, HTV-X becomes the fourth cargo resupply vehicle serving the International Space Station, joining Russia's Progress, Northrop Grumman's Cygnus, and SpaceX's Dragon in supporting orbital operations.

media:content.media:title: Japan's HTV-X Cargo Vehicle Launches First Mission to International Space Station

item.title: Newly Discovered Asteroid 2025 TP5 Passes Closer Than the Moon: Earth's Near-Miss Event
item.dc:creator: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) & ATLAS Survey System
item.description: On October 13, 2025, the ATLAS (Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System) telescope at Mauna Loa, Hawaii, discovered a remarkable near-Earth asteroid designated 2025 TP5. Measuring approximately 16 meters (54 feet) in diameter—comparable to a 6-story building and similar in size to the 2013 Chelyabinsk meteor—this asteroid passed within 97,089 kilometers of Earth on October 15, 2025, making it closer than the Moon's orbital distance of 384,000 kilometers.

media:content.media:title: Newly Discovered Asteroid 2025 TP5 Passes Closer Than the Moon: Earth's Near-Miss Event
